summary: Inverting a newly added gate revealed it was redundant rather than load-bearing: an existing fixture already asserted a strictly stronger property, so the new assertion could never have been the first to fail.
evidence: file:tests/SIR.Conformance.Shared/SpatialQueryFixtures.fs line 78 require (cache1 = cache2) 'Cache hit mutated cache state.'; command:dotnet run --project tests/SIR.Domain.Tests -c Release -- (with evaluateCached mutated to shadow a hit) -> failed with the PRE-EXISTING message, not the new one
cost: none - the inversion pass caught it before the PR, and the redundant assertion was removed rather than shipped
owner: EHotwagner/S.I.R. - pnext-item gate-inversion rule (it detects redundant gates, not only vacuous ones)

summary: A performance harness that ran four workloads in one process manufactured two reproducible false regressions of roughly 2x in the workloads that ran last, in code those workloads never executed.
evidence: command:dotnet run --project tests/SIR.PhysicalCombat.Performance -c Release -- --working-set (four workloads, one process) reported cache 7.0->11.5us and tick 4.9->7.5ms as regressions across 4 interleaved rounds; command:same binary with --working-set f3 and --working-set f1f6 one workload per process reported cache 11.5->11.7us (neutral) and tick 10.2->7.4ms (1.38x faster); file:tests/SIR.PhysicalCombat.Performance/Program.fs
cost: roughly a dozen build-and-measure cycles and four discarded redesigns of a boundary resolver that was never the cause
